# Accessibility

Curated by Skill Harbor: a practical accessibility skill for designing, implementing, and auditing interfaces to WCAG 2.2 Level AA across Web, iOS, and Android. It works through the POUR principles (Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust) as a five-step implementation flow: identify the component role (semantic native elements first), define perceivable attributes (4.5:1 contrast, text alternatives, 400% reflow), implement operable controls (24x24px minimum targets, visible focus, keyboard reachability), ensure understandable logic (consistent navigation, descriptive errors, no redundant entry), and verify robust compatibility (correct Name/Role/Value, live regions). The standout asset is its cross-platform mapping table: every pattern is given in HTML/ARIA, SwiftUI (accessibilityLabel, traits, hints), and Jetpack Compose (semantics, contentDescription) side by side, with copy-paste examples for each. An anti-patterns section names the usual sins (div-buttons, color-only meaning, unfocused modals, redundant alt text) and a best-practices checklist closes the loop. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: it implements the technical side of WCAG, it does not replace testing with real assistive-technology users; platform APIs evolve, spot-check generated attributes against current docs. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
